title: Extending Regular Indifferentiability for Two-Permutation Sums
summary: Regular indifferentiability for the sum of two public permutations is proved up to a query bound of two raised to two n over three and divided by n; proving a larger bound remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the sum of two public permutations, determine whether regular indifferentiability can be proved with a query bound strictly greater than $2^{2n/3}/n$. The currently reattained result establishes regular indifferentiability up to $2^{2n/3}/n$ queries using the Mennink--Preneel simulator, query shuffling, and a sequential-indifferentiability result as a black box; the query-shuffling argument is valid only up to that bound. The unresolved task is to surpass $2^{2n/3}/n$ by overcoming the simulator-query-shuffling and sequential-indifferentiability bottlenecks, potentially through a more sophisticated simulator or an entirely different proof approach.

scope.domain: Symmetric-cryptographic indifferentiability of the sum of two public permutations.
parameters: n: size parameter governing the query bound
Number of queries: resource threshold whose bound is to be improved
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether regular indifferentiability can be proved beyond $2^{2n/3}/n$ queries despite the simulator, query-shuffling, and sequential-indifferentiability bottlenecks.

citations.label: Revisiting the Indifferentiability of the Sum of Permutations

progress.summary: The source reattains the stated query bound using the Mennink–Preneel simulator, query shuffling, and sequential indifferentiability as a black box. It suggests that exceeding the bound may require a more sophisticated simulator or a different proof approach.
